body:
FOUND AT T64'S LANDING (#266): `Gateway.cut`, `slates()`, `receipt()`, `graveyards()` are public methods whose parameter and return types — SlateReport, CutReport, RestoreReport's siblings, the graveyard/receipt shapes, the slate claim builders — are not exported from `src/index.ts`. A consumer of the published package can call the doors and cannot NAME what they answer, except by deep dist/ import. This is exactly T82's defect (the container surface after T32) recurring one arc later, and the rule from that landing applies verbatim: export THE DOOR AND THE VOCABULARY A CALLER NEEDS TO DESCRIBE, SIGN, AND READ WHAT THE DOOR ANSWERS — and deliberately NOT the `*Impl` seams.

Also apply T82's other two disciplines: probe the NEGATIVE (export an Impl on purpose, watch the surface rail fail, revert — so 'we don't ship the internals' is pinned rather than assumed), and extend `pack.test.ts`'s dist expectations for the new d.ts files the re-exports resolve through.

The capabilities book's §29 claims currently name `Gateway` as their door — honest today. When this lands, sharpen them to the named exports in the same PR, or the book undersells a surface that exists.

Self-merge bar: repair-tier (restores the stated T82 rule for a landed surface), on green + P5 + the negative probe.
title: The slate surface is public methods with unexported vocabulary — T82's defect, one arc later
